source_name: ČNB – ARAD time series, supervisory statistics & payment-system statistics
why_relevant: ARAD is the regulator's public time-series database, and ČNB explicitly publishes selected supervisory statistics through it (entity counts and basic financial statements under 'Basic Financial Market Indicators') alongside harmonised, non-confidential payment statistics. For a source-scouting pass this matters because it supplies the sector denominator against which any individual second-tier bank's disclosed numbers can be normalised, and it covers payment-instrument and channel aggregates that individual challenger banks never break out. Machine-friendly time series, so it is a genuinely low-cost long-term collection target.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace – ČBA Online & ČBA Monitor (sector statistics, Hypomonitor, expert outputs)
why_relevant: The industry association aggregates 'basic indicators on the development of the domestic banking sector' explicitly built from ČNB statistics plus the mandatory published data of individual banks — i.e. it does part of the cross-bank normalisation work for this cell already, including for the smaller banks whose figures are otherwise scattered across ad hoc XLSX annexes. It also runs ČBA Hypomonitor (mortgage market), a quarterly forecasting panel drawn from member-bank economists, and a press/news stream. Additionally, the 'ČBA standard' quarterly disclosure format is what several banks in this cell (Partners Banka, Max banka) name for their capital-adequacy filings, so the association is also the format authority.

source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha (Prague Stock Exchange) – MONETA issuer detail & news
source_subtype: stock exchange issuer page / market data
why_relevant: The exchange-side record for the cell's only listed bank: price and volume history, order book, market makers, a corporate calendar carrying shareholder meetings and financial-results announcement dates, dividend history with ex-date and record date, and a news tab carrying PSE and ČTK announcements. Useful as an independent confirmation of MONETA's reporting calendar and corporate actions, and as the market's real-time reaction signal to disclosures — a dimension no corporate source provides. Structured products written on MONETA shares are also listed here, an indirect indicator of retail interest.

source_name: Patria.cz – regulated-information / issuer news feed (Czech financial wire)
source_subtype: financial newswire carrying issuer regulatory notices
why_relevant: Patria carries verbatim issuer regulated-information notices for Czech bond and equity issuers — the 'Banka CREDITAS a.s.: Výroční finanční zpráva za rok 2025' item is a filing notice, not journalism. This makes it a practical redundant path to filings from issuers whose own sites are bot-defended (CREDITAS returned 403 to a direct fetch) and a low-friction way to detect that a filing has occurred, with a timestamp. Numeric article ids make the archive enumerable.

source_name: Czech retail-finance comparison & watchdog portals (Měšec.cz, Peníze.cz, Finparáda, Zlatá koruna, Banky.cz)
source_subtype: consumer-finance trade press / product comparison aggregator
why_relevant: These portals systematically track exactly the disclosures this cell's banks make thinnest: fee-schedule changes, savings and term-deposit repricing, product launches, and structural events. Observed coverage in this session included Partners Banka's multi-currency account and in-app bitcoin offering, MONETA fee changes, the Max banka–CREDITAS merger mechanics and deposit-insurance consequences, Hello bank's wind-down, and CREDITAS's record 2025 profit — often with more operational detail than the banks' own releases. Peníze.cz additionally maintains a financial-subject database and a bank-ownership overview, useful for actor-map validation. Treat as corroboration and lead-generation, never as a primary citation.

source_name: Garanční systém finančního trhu – deposit guarantee scheme notices
source_subtype: deposit guarantee scheme / statutory safety-net body
why_relevant: The Czech deposit guarantee scheme publishes bank-specific notices at exactly the moments that matter structurally — mergers (its Creditas/Max banka page explains the combined EUR 100,000 limit and the three-month penalty-free withdrawal window), wind-downs and licence events. These notices are legally precise about effective dates, making them a better dating source for structural events than press coverage, and they identify which banks share a guarantee limit, which is itself an ownership-structure signal.

source_name: Global Payments Europe, s.r.o. — Sbírka listin (Collection of Deeds), Veřejný rejstřík
why_relevant: Global Payments Europe, s.r.o. (IČO 27088936, V olšinách 626/80, Praha 10, incorporated 2003-09-24, ex-MUZO a.s.) is the Prague card-processing centre serving issuers and acquirers across CEE. Czech law obliges it to file full statutory annual reports (účetní závěrka + výroční zpráva) into the Sbírka listin. This is the single most authoritative disclosure channel for its revenue, headcount, related-party flows to Global Payments Inc. and auditor commentary — none of which appears in the US parent's segment reporting.

source_name: Global Payments s.r.o. (Czech merchant acquiring arm) — Sbírka listin
why_relevant: Separate legal entity from the processing centre: Global Payments s.r.o., IČO 04235452, same address (V olšinách 626/80, Praha 10), incorporated 2015-07-10, NACE 64999 (other financial services). This is the vehicle through which Global Payments runs Czech merchant acquiring after the Erste/Česká spořitelna acquiring relationship. Splitting processing (27088936) from acquiring (04235452) in the accounts is what lets you separate 'Prague as a regional processing hub' from 'Czech acquiring market share'.

source_name: Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o. — Sbírka listin
why_relevant: IČO 03633144, Rohanské nábřeží 670/17, Karlín, Praha 8, incorporated 2014-12-10, NACE 64999/46190. This is the Czech operating entity behind the KB SmartPay acquiring joint venture with Komerční banka (a public RM-SYSTEM notice records KB selling a 1% stake in this exact entity, confirming the shared-ownership structure). Its statutory accounts are the only place the Czech acquiring JV's economics are visible; Worldline SA group reporting does not break out Czechia.

source_name: Nexi Czech Republic, s.r.o. — Sbírka listin
why_relevant: IČO 27391761, V celnici 1031/4, Nové Město, Praha 1, incorporated 2005-10-31. Confirms Nexi (post Nets/SIA consolidation) has a live Czech legal entity — a fact not visible from any Czech-language Nexi web presence. Because Nexi publishes nothing locally, the statutory filings are effectively the only Czech-side disclosure on its footprint here, and the register's history section is where a rename from an earlier SIA/Nets brand would be recorded.

source_name: ARES — Administrativní registr ekonomických subjektů (REST API)
why_relevant: The entity-resolution backbone for this whole cell. A clean, unauthenticated JSON REST API from the Ministry of Finance: GET by IČO returns legal name, registered address, incorporation date, NACE codes and active-registration flags; POST /vyhledat searches by trade name. This is how you enumerate 'who actually is an acquirer/processor registered in Czechia' rather than guessing from marketing sites, and how you detect new entrants, renames and liquidations. It resolved every actor in this cell (Global Payments Europe 27088936, Global Payments s.r.o. 04235452, Worldline CZ 03633144, Nexi CZ 27391761, Comgate 27924505, MONET+ 26217783, Ingenico CZ 28869591, Euronet Services 25608452, Adyen N.V. CZ representative 19640706).

source_name: Veřejný rejstřík a Sbírka listin — company search entry point (justice.cz)
why_relevant: The search front-end that maps IČO to the internal subjektId needed for every deeds URL, and that exposes the full register extract (statutory bodies, shareholders, branch offices, 'ostatní skutečnosti'). Snowballing from here turns one known acquirer into its trade unions, branches and affiliated entities — e.g. 'Odborová organizace Worldline Czech Republic' at the same Karlín address, a signal of local headcount scale.

source_name: Global Payments Inc. — Investor Relations press releases
why_relevant: Parent-level newsroom for the owner of the Prague processing centre. Contract wins, platform migrations, divestitures and regional restructurings that touch Czechia are announced here long before any Czech-language communication appears — and often are never communicated locally at all. Confirmed live with a dated, per-item permalink structure (/press-releases/detail/<id>/<slug>).

source_name: Global Payments Inc. — SEC filings and annual report / proxy archive
why_relevant: Audited, legally binding disclosure for the parent. 10-K risk factors and segment notes occasionally name CEE processing operations, restructuring charges and data-centre consolidations that explain what happens to the Prague site. Direct PDF/XBRL asset URLs are exposed on the index, making this cheaply machine-collectable.

source_name: Worldline — Media relations / newsroom
why_relevant: Group newsroom of the operator of Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o. and the KB SmartPay JV. Bank re-platforming deals, acquiring JV changes and divestitures across Europe are announced here; given Worldline's ongoing portfolio reshaping, this is the highest-signal early-warning channel for changes affecting the Czech acquiring JV.

source_name: Worldline — Investor Relations news & events
why_relevant: Regulated-information channel for Worldline SA (Euronext). Divestiture announcements, contract renewals with banks and segment commentary land here with legal precision that the marketing newsroom lacks. Complements the Czech statutory accounts of Worldline Czech Republic s.r.o.

source_name: KB SmartPay — Czech acquiring JV commercial site and document library
why_relevant: The customer-facing brand of the Komerční banka / Worldline Czech Republic acquiring joint venture. Its Czech-language terms-and-conditions PDFs (including 'zvláštní podmínky' for interchange and for hotel merchants) are published under a stable /content/dam/kb-smartpay/documents/ path and are dated — meaning pricing-model and scheme-fee changes are observable in the open without any commercial subscription. That is an unusually direct read on Czech acquiring economics.

source_name: ČSOB — platbakartou.csob.cz (bank acquiring arm site and blog)
why_relevant: ČSOB runs its card-acceptance business on a dedicated domain with its own blog, separate from the main csob.cz corporate site (which returned HTTP 500 on the press paths tried). Product launches such as software-POS and gateway-free online acceptance are announced on this blog rather than in bank press releases, so it is the practical channel for tracking a major Czech bank acquiring arm.

source_name: Global Payments Česko — globalpayments.cz (Czech commercial site, blog and document library)
why_relevant: The Czech-language public face of Global Payments' acquiring and terminal business, including a blog that carries operational/regulatory notices to merchants (e.g. a PSD2 parameter-migration notice) and a 'Důležité dokumenty ke stažení' library of contractual terms. These merchant-facing notices are the best open signal of platform migrations and scheme-mandate implementation dates in Czechia.

source_name: GP webpay — gpwebpay.cz (Global Payments Europe payment gateway)
why_relevant: GP webpay is the e-commerce gateway operated out of the Prague Global Payments Europe entity and embedded in a large share of Czech e-shops. Its technical documentation, API changelogs and merchant integration notices are the clearest published trace of what the Prague processing platform actually supports — 3-D Secure versions, scheme mandates, tokenisation — which in turn indicates the platform generation banks are buying into.

source_name: Sdružení pro bankovní karty (SBK) — bankovnikarty.cz
why_relevant: The Czech bank-card industry association: the single best pointer source for this cell. It aggregates the actor map (banks, acquirers, processors, scheme representatives), publishes quarterly market statistics on card counts, terminal counts, e-commerce and cashback volumes, and hosts the industry's press-release archive. It also anchors the events ecosystem (Acquiring Day, Card Forum) where acquiring contracts and processor switches are discussed publicly. The site is current — it links a Visa press release dated August 2026.

source_name: SBK press-release archive — aktuality.bankovnikarty.cz
why_relevant: A long-running, flat-file archive of Czech card-industry press releases — SBK quarterly market releases, scheme statements (Visa, Mastercard), regulator/arbiter statements, and vendor announcements including a dated Ingenico release. Because it is plain HTML with dated PDF filenames it is trivially harvestable and gives multi-year time depth on who announced what in Czech card acquiring and processing.

source_name: CardMag — Czech card-industry trade magazine and PDF archive
why_relevant: The specialist Czech trade magazine for cards and payments, published in the same stable as SBK. Its freely downloadable back-issue PDFs carry interviews with processor and acquirer executives, market-share commentary, and coverage of the MUZO to Global Payments Europe lineage — the kind of institutional history that no corporate site retains. Excellent for reconstructing which bank moved its card processing where, and when.

source_name: Acquiring Day — Czech acquiring industry conference
why_relevant: A conference dedicated specifically to card acquiring in the Czech/CEE market, run from the SBK/CardMag stable. Agendas and speaker lists are a compact, self-updating actor map of who currently matters in Czech acquiring and processing — including vendors and processors that never issue press releases. Historical programme PDFs are hosted on the SBK site.

source_name: Card Forum — cardforum.cz
why_relevant: The second event property in the Czech card ecosystem, complementing Acquiring Day with broader card/issuing coverage. Same value proposition: programme and speaker lists reveal the current roster of Czech processors, acquirers and their bank counterparties, and flag emerging vendors before they appear in trade press.

source_name: ČNB JERRS — Jednotný registr regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů
why_relevant: The Czech National Bank's authoritative register of licensed and registered financial-market entities, including payment institutions (platební instituce), small-scale payment service providers and their EU passporting notifications. Determines which acquirers/PSPs are locally licensed versus passporting in from another member state — a structural fact that decides who can actually contract with Czech banks and merchants, and that no commercial database gets consistently right.

source_name: ČNB — Statistika platebního styku (payment systems statistics and methodology)
why_relevant: Official harmonised statistics on Czech payment infrastructure — numbers of cards, POS terminals, ATMs and transaction volumes/values, with a published methodological note. This is the denominator against which any acquirer's or processor's claimed share must be checked, and the terminal-count series is the closest public proxy for acquiring-market growth. Independent of the industry association's own figures, so useful as a cross-check on SBK data.

source_name: ČTK Protext — Czech news agency paid press-release wire
why_relevant: Protext is the ČTK channel through which Czech companies and associations push full-text press releases into the national news feed. SBK's quarterly card-market releases were found here with stable per-item permalinks (/zpravy/show/<id>), and it is a common route for payment vendors' Czech announcements. Being a wire, it captures releases from firms with no usable newsroom of their own — exactly the gap for Nexi and the smaller processors.

source_name: České noviny (ČTK) — Tiskové zprávy section
why_relevant: The public-facing ČTK site that republishes wire press releases with durable numeric permalinks, including SBK card-market releases. Complements Protext with a second, differently-indexed copy of the same corpus — valuable because Czech corporate press releases frequently disappear from company sites but persist here.

source_name: Comgate a.s. — independent Czech acquirer/PSP (site plus Sbírka listin)
why_relevant: IČO 27924505, Gočárova třída 1754/48b, Hradec Králové, incorporated 2007-07-16. The most prominent domestically-owned challenger in Czech card acceptance, competing directly with the bank-and-international-processor incumbents on terminal and gateway pricing. Its published obchodní podmínky carry explicit effective dates, making its pricing moves datable, and its statutory accounts show whether the price aggression is funded by growth or losses.

source_name: MONET+, a.s. — Czech card technology and processing vendor (Sbírka listin)
why_relevant: IČO 26217783, Za Dvorem 505, Štípa, Zlín, incorporated 2000-06-30. A domestically-owned supplier of card/smartcard and payment technology to Czech and regional banks — the kind of vendor whose customer wins are a leading indicator of bank card-platform decisions but which issues almost no press. Statutory accounts plus the register's history are the reliable trace of its scale and ownership.

source_name: Ingenico CZ s.r.o. — terminal vendor Czech entity (Sbírka listin)
why_relevant: IČO 28869591, Lazarská 11/6, Praha 2, incorporated 2009-04-06. The Czech arm of the dominant POS terminal vendor. Terminal-estate refresh cycles and Android-POS migrations are decided jointly with acquirers, so this entity's revenue trajectory is a proxy for Czech acquiring capex. A dated Ingenico press release also sits in the SBK archive, showing this actor does communicate locally.

source_name: Nexi Group — press releases and financial press releases
why_relevant: The only functioning newsroom for the Nexi/Nets group, whose Czech legal entity (Nexi Czech Republic, s.r.o., IČO 27391761) publishes nothing locally. Group-level announcements are therefore the sole narrative channel for what Nexi intends in this market, including any CEE acquiring or issuer-processing contract. The separate financial press-release feed under Investor Relations carries the regulated-disclosure versions.

source_name: Euronet — Czech operations news (euronetatms.cz) and Euronet Services spol. s r.o.
why_relevant: Euronet Services, spol. s r.o. (IČO 25608452, Pobřežní 3, Praha 8, incorporated 1997-09-16) is a long-established independent ATM and payments operator in Czechia, and Euronet has been actively buying bank merchant-acquiring portfolios in Europe. Its Czech site republishes group announcements in a Czech context — one observed item covers Euronet acquiring a bank's merchant-acquiring business — making it a live indicator of the 'bank exits acquiring' pattern this cell tracks.

source_name: Registr smluv — Czech public contracts register (smlouvy.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Czech law requires state bodies, municipalities and state-owned enterprises to publish contracts above a threshold in full text. Card-acceptance and processing contracts signed by public-sector merchants (transport operators, hospitals, Česká pošta, ministries) therefore become public documents naming the acquirer, the pricing and the term — a rare open window on real acquiring economics that no vendor would disclose voluntarily. A Komerční banka contract record was observed in search results, confirming banks' contracts do land here.

source_name: NEN — Národní elektronický nástroj (public procurement portal)
why_relevant: Tenders for card-acceptance, terminal supply and payment-processing services run by Czech public contracting authorities are published here with specifications, bidder lists and award decisions. Award notices name the winning acquirer/processor and the contract value — the clearest hard evidence of competitive position available in this market, and an early signal when a public-sector merchant re-tenders and switches provider.

source_name: Lupa.cz — Czech internet and e-commerce/payments trade press
why_relevant: Covers the e-commerce payments layer — gateways, PSPs, softPOS and platform switches — which is where Czech acquiring competition is currently most visible. Also carries a tiskové zprávy channel that captures vendor announcements not published elsewhere. Complements Měšec.cz's consumer/fees angle with a technology-and-platform angle relevant to processing decisions.

source_name: Comgate a.s. — Pro média (press room, tiskové zprávy + výroční zprávy)
why_relevant: Official press room of Comgate a.s. (IČ 279 24 505, Hradec Králové), a Czech-licensed European payment institution running one of the largest CZ payment gateways plus ~10k physical terminals. The page carries dated tiskové zprávy as downloadable PDF/DOCX files (tz-2024-11-26.pdf, tz-2024-11-05.docx, tz-2024-06-18.pdf, tz-2024-01-31.pdf, tz-2023-10-24.pdf, tz-2023-04-20.pdf, tz-2023-02-01.pdf) AND a set of downloadable company annual reports (výroční zprávy) covering 2020-2024, plus a press contact and a 'Zmínili se o nás' media-mentions index. This is a rare case of a CZ payment institution publishing both marketing disclosures and statutory annual reports in one place, and the releases reference merchant surveys and e-commerce performance comparisons — i.e. payment-mix and merchant-behaviour signal ahead of bank/regulator reporting.

source_name: Comgate — Blog o platebních službách (product + case-study blog)
why_relevant: Comgate's product and merchant-case-study blog. Observed dated posts include 'Dynamické řízení 3D Secure pro více dokončených plateb' (2026-07-29), 'Comgate Web Checkout: Platba kartou v košíku' (2026-05-29), 'Mobilní checkout v aplikaci pro Android a iOS' (2026-05-21) and 'Rok 2025 v Comgate' (2026-01-23), the last of which discusses growth in payment volume and client count. Named merchant case studies (Colours of Ostrava, TASY, Topgal, Pytloun Hotels, Bosonožka, Zdravotní klaun) are direct merchant-win evidence. Useful for tracking checkout-technology roadmap (3DS risk-based routing, in-cart card payment, in-app checkout) and for building a merchant-logo map.

source_name: GoPay — Tiskové zprávy (press release category on the GoPay blog)
why_relevant: The actual press-release archive of GoPay, which operates in CZ as 'GoPay Czech odštěpný závod' and is part of the Worldline group. Observed dated releases carry exactly the kind of quantified payments intelligence this cell exists to capture: 'GoPay spouští odložené platby přes Twisto a Skip Pay' (2024-10-29, BNPL rails added to the gateway), 'GoPay spustí odložené platby' (2024-06-05), the Worldline rebrand (2022-11-16), 'GoPay pokračuje v rekordním růstu' (2021-03-17), and the Worldline acquisition (2020-09-09). Stated figures include 'more than 18,000 e-shops' in CZ+SK and a 2025 target of CZK 90 billion transaction volume with double-digit revenue growth. GoPay self-describes as the largest provider of online payments of Czech origin.

source_name: GoPay — Pro média (press contact + headline metrics)
why_relevant: GoPay's media landing page. Names the press contact (Jan Vodička, CMO, jan.vodicka@gopay.cz), states 'more than 11 thousand merchants' across Central Europe and annual transaction volume 'in billions of CZK', and lists reference clients (Skylink, Voyo, O2, Kytary.cz, Footshop, Fortuna, Wedos) — a directly usable merchant-win list. It also routes to the case-study archive. Note the merchant-count figure here (11k, Central Europe) differs from the 18k CZ+SK figure in the press releases; that discrepancy is itself worth tracking as a definitional signal.

source_name: GoPay — Účetní závěrky 2020-2024 (statutory financial statements, published on O nás)
why_relevant: GoPay's 'O nás' page publishes downloadable účetní závěrky (financial statements) for 2020-2024 as PDFs served from site.gopaycdn.com, and lays out the ČNB licensing history: 2007 small-scope financial services (poskytování finančních služeb malého rozsahu), 2012 payment-services/EMI-level licence, 2019 PSD2 services. That licence timeline plus the annual financials give a hard, auditable series for revenue and volume on a CZ payment institution that otherwise discloses only marketing numbers. The CZ operating form is an odštěpný závod (branch), which matters for how the statutory filings are structured.

source_name: ThePay, a.s. — corporate site (thepay.eu, formerly thepay.cz)
why_relevant: ThePay, a.s. (IČO 28135261, DIČ CZ28135261, Masarykovo náměstí 102/65, Jihlava) is one of the four domestic CZ gateway brands named in this cell. The old thepay.cz domain now 301-redirects to thepay.eu, itself a signal of a CEE-wide repositioning worth noting. Critically, on the pages inspected (homepage, /cs/kontakt/) there is NO blog, novinky or tiskové zprávy section — ThePay's public communications footprint is thin, so intelligence on it must come from statutory filings (Sbírka listin under IČO 28135261) and third-party press rather than from the company itself. Footer routes: /cs/napoveda/, /cs/kontakt/, /cs/pdf-verze/, /cs/partnersky-program-thepay/.

source_name: PayU Czech — Zprávy a média (CZ newsroom)
why_relevant: PayU's Czech-language newsroom, self-described as covering 'Novinky z oblasti fintech, e-commerce trendy a rozhovory'. This is the localised counterpart to PayU's global corporate newsroom and the only PayU channel likely to carry CZ-specific merchant wins, local payment-method launches (bank transfers, Google Pay/Apple Pay, BNPL) and CZ e-commerce commentary. PayU has 20+ years in CEE and runs country sites for CZ, PL, HU and RO, so cross-country comparison is possible from a single operator's disclosures.

source_name: PayU Global (corporate) — Media and press / News
why_relevant: PayU's group-level newsroom. Observed dated releases: 'PayU GPO optimisation tools fuel merchant growth' (Mar 2025), 'Redefining Peak Sales Days' (Jan 2025), 'PayU GPO integrates with Google Pay' (Dec 2024), and a CRO appointment (Jul 2024). None are CZ-specific, but GPO (Global Payment Organisation) platform announcements propagate into the Czech product set, and 'peak sales day' analyses cover CEE merchant behaviour. Use as the upstream feed for product/rail changes that will surface in CZ. Press enquiries route via /media-and-press/press-enquires/. No RSS feed observed.

source_name: Besteron — CZ blog and company page (besteron.com/cz)
why_relevant: Besteron is a Slovak-licensed payment institution ('Besteron A.S.', approved and regulated by Národná banka Slovenska, permit ODB-6111/2015-7) selling actively into the Czech market — a live example of the SK-licence / CZ-market passporting pattern this cell must track. Company facts observed on /cz/o-nas/: founded 2014, 4 European markets, 6,100+ clients, Tapeon acquisition and Seyfor becoming majority owner in 2021, Slovenia entry 2022, Croatia entry 2025. CZ helpdesk helpdesk@besteron.cz, +420 910 920 720. There is no dedicated press room; the blog and the webinar/academy section (/cz/webinare/) are the communication channels. The Seyfor ownership link is notable — it ties the gateway to a large CZ/SK business-software group.

source_name: GP webpay (Global Payments Europe, s.r.o.) — Novinky
why_relevant: MAJOR ACTOR MISSING FROM THE SEED LIST, found by snowballing. GP webpay is operated by Global payments Europe, s.r.o. (V Olšinách 626/80, Praha 10 - Strašnice) and self-describes as 'nejpoužívanější platební brána v českých e-shopech' (the most-used payment gateway in Czech e-shops). It is the gateway sitting behind much of CZ bank card acquiring, so its novinky feed is arguably the single highest-leverage gateway news source in the country for card-acceptance changes, 3DS mandates and scheme rule rollouts. Any CZ payment-gateway landscape that omits GP webpay is structurally incomplete.

source_name: Twisto — Pro média (press room)
why_relevant: Twisto is a CZ-licensed payment institution and the BNPL rail now embedded inside CZ gateways (confirmed by GoPay's 2024-10-29 release adding Twisto and Skip Pay as odložené platby). Its press room carries dated releases from 2018 through January 2026 — market expansion (Bulgaria entry Dec 2025), consumer financial-behaviour surveys, product launches and milestones — plus a press kit and press contact pr@twisto.cz. Historical figures observed include 'odložená platba po vyzkoušení' on 'více než 17 tisíc e-shopů' and 600,000 Czech users as of June 2019. Twisto self-describes as the CZ BNPL market leader. Its survey releases are a recurring source of consumer-side payment-behaviour data.
